newsitem.title: JAPAN: Uzbek '96 cotton output to fall short of target - PM.
newsitem.headline: Uzbek '96 cotton output to fall short of target - PM.

text.p: Uzbekistan's Prime Minister Utkur Sultanov said on Monday his country was unable to meet its target in this year's cotton harvest.
"We were 320,000 tonnes short," the prime minister said at a news conference in Tokyo.
Sources at the Agriculture Ministry of the Central Asian country had said in October that Uzbekistan expected to harvest around four million tonnes of raw cotton in 1996.
Uzbekistan is the world's fourth-largest producer and the second-largest exporter of cotton.
Sultanov also said his country will try to grow a different type of cotton using a new method that will increase the harvest in 1997.
"We will try seeds that mature faster and produce more cotton," he said.
"The agricultural technique that we will adopt consists of covering the soil with film after planting the seeds to avoid drastic changes in temperature," he added.

The main buyers of Uzbek cotton are Switzerland, Britain, the Netherlands, South Korea, Turkey and Austria. Sultanov, on a seven-day visit to Tokyo until December 21, is to meet with Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda and business leaders.
